stories.title: Nasza historia
stories.text: Przed założeniem Moniré poznałyśmy się jako frontend developerki w brack.ch, jednym z największych sklepów internetowych w Szwajcarii. Nasze drogi do świata technologii były dalekie od typowych. Monika wywodzi się z HR i konsultingu, a Nikky wcześniej pracowała jako lekarka weterynarii. To właśnie te różnorodne doświadczenia stały się naszą wspólną siłą. Nie tylko tworzymy strony internetowe i piszemy kod. Rozumiemy wyzwania biznesowe z różnych perspektyw. Dlatego założyłyśmy Moniré: dla firm, które szukają czegoś więcej niż tylko technicznej realizacji. Szukają prawdziwej współpracy i partnerów, którzy myślą razem z nimi.

stories.title: Dlaczego duo?
stories.text: Pracując z nami, otrzymujesz uwagę i troskę butikowej agencji z doświadczeniem profesjonalistek. Żadnych warstw zarządzania, żadnego outsourcingu — tylko dwie zaangażowane założycielki, którym zależy na Twoim sukcesie.

stories.title: Działalność społeczna
stories.text: Za każdy płatny projekt tworzymy darmową lub mocno przecenioną stronę dla organizacji charytatywnej, non-profit lub inicjatywy społecznej.

items.a: Musimy zrozumieć Twoje cele biznesowe, grupę docelową, potrzebne funkcje, preferencje designu, harmonogram i budżet. Jeśli masz istniejące materiały marki, treści lub strony, to również pomoże. Wypełnij nasz formularz briefu klienta, abyśmy mogli lepiej zrozumieć Twoje potrzeby.
Nasz główny focus to rozwój i automatyzacja AI, ale budujemy strony z uwzględnieniem najlepszych praktyk SEO. Możemy też polecić zaufanych partnerów do bieżących usług SEO.
Tak! Mamy siedzibę w Szwajcarii i pracujemy zdalnie z klientami na całym świecie. Komunikacja jest przyjazna asynchronicznie, a spotkania dostosowujemy do różnych stref czasowych.

items.q: Czy budujecie indywidualne strony czy korzystacie z szablonów?
items.a: Budujemy głównie indywidualne strony dostosowane do Twoich potrzeb. Możemy jednak również dostosować premium szablony, jeśli pracujesz z mniejszym budżetem lub krótszym terminem.

items.q: Czy możecie przeprojektować moją istniejącą stronę?
items.a: Tak! Oferujemy kompletne redesigny stron, w tym modernizację przestarzałych projektów, poprawę doświadczenia użytkownika i migrację na nowe platformy.

Pracujemy z różnymi technologiami, w tym Webflow, Astro, React, Next.js, n8n i rozwiązaniami na zamówienie. Rekomendujemy najlepszą platformę na podstawie Twoich wymagań, budżetu i celów długoterminowych.
Używamy przyjaznych systemów zarządzania treścią (CMS), dzięki czemu możesz aktualizować teksty, obrazy i posty na blogu bez umiejętności technicznych. Zapewniamy szkolenie i dokumentację.
Po opłaceniu wszystkich faktur, pełne prawa własności do strony i wszystkich stworzonych przez nas projektów są przenoszone na Ciebie.

items.q: Mam projekt graficzny – czy możecie zająć się tylko programowaniem?
items.a: Jeśli masz już projekt graficzny, możemy zająć się tylko programowaniem. Omówimy Twój projekt wspólnie i dostosujemy wycenę do potrzebnych prac.

items.q: Jak szybko może być gotowa moja strona?
items.a: Terminy różnią się w zależności od wielkości i złożoności strony. Po wstępnej rozmowie podamy jasne szacunki dla faz projektowania i programowania.
Webflow to nowoczesna platforma do budowy stron, która pozwala nam tworzyć w pełni indywidualne, wysokiej jakości strony szybko – z łatwą edycją, świetną wydajnością i bezproblemowym hostingiem.

items.q: Czym jest automatyzacja AI i jak może pomóc mojej firmie?
items.a: Automatyzacja AI wykorzystuje sztuczną inteligencję do obsługi powtarzalnych zadań, analizy danych lub usprawniania procesów. Przykłady to chatboty obsługi klienta, wprowadzanie danych, tworzenie odpowiedzi e-mail, generowanie treści i więcej. Celem jest umożliwienie Ci skupienia się na wartościowej pracy i redukcja błędów.

items.q: Jakich narzędzi używacie do tworzenia automatyzacji?
items.a: Najczęściej tworzymy automatyzacje w n8n, które łączy się z narzędziami używanymi już przez wiele firm, takimi jak e-mail, arkusze kalkulacyjne, przechowywanie plików w chmurze i systemy CRM. Korzystamy też z narzędzi AI, takich jak Claude i OpenAI Codex, aby wspierać development i tworzyć bardziej dopasowane rozwiązania. W niektórych projektach dobieramy inne narzędzia, jeśli lepiej pasują do celu.

items.q: Czy potrzebuję wiedzy technicznej, żeby korzystać z narzędzi AI?
items.a: Nie! Projektujemy przyjazne rozwiązania, które płynnie integrują się z Twoimi istniejącymi procesami. Zapewniamy szkolenie i dokumentację, abyś mógł pewnie korzystać z narzędzi.
Oferujemy pakiety utrzymania obejmujące poprawki błędów, aktualizacje treści i wsparcie techniczne. Oferujemy również jednorazowe wsparcie dla konkretnych potrzeb.

cta.title: Zainteresowany współpracą?
cta.subtext: Pracujemy jednocześnie z ograniczoną liczbą klientów, aby każdy projekt otrzymał uwagę, na jaką zasługuje.

snip-squad.title: Snip Squad
snip-squad.subtitle: A modern, approachable website for a nonprofit veterinary clinic

sections.title: Overview:
sections.intro:
Snip Squad is a nonprofit veterinary clinic in Norfolk, Virginia providing affordable care for pets in underserved communities.

They needed a website that clearly communicates their mission, supports donations, and helps visitors quickly find key information.

sections.title: Approach:
sections.intro:
Snip Squad wanted to move away from the typical clinical look and create something more modern, friendly, and community-focused.

We focused on:
items: A warm, approachable visual style
Clear, structured, easy-to-scan content
A fully responsive experience across mobile, tablet, and desktop
An easy-to-manage CMS for the team

sections.title: Outcome:
sections.intro: The result is a clean, welcoming digital presence that reflects Snip Squad’s mission and supports both service discovery and donations.

testimonial.quote: What an incredible website designer!! From start to finish they made it easy to make my dreams come true. Sometimes it can be overwhelming to even start and figure out what your vision would be for your website but Monire was able to speak with me and help me create the vision that I wanted for my website/business. In this day and age website design is so important and I would choose Monire 10/10 times to work with. Great team with excellent deadline times and easy to work with during modification process. portco-hr-collective.title: PortCo HR Collective
portco-hr-collective.subtitle: An exclusive membership platform for HR leaders in private equity
portco-hr-collective.category: Branding, Web Design & Development, AI Automation

sections.title: Overview:
sections.intro: PortCo HR Collective is a peer network for Chief HR Officers working in PE-backed companies across Europe. The founders wanted a platform that felt professional, welcoming, and distinctly their own. Not a generic platform, but a professional digital home that could establish credibility, support growth, and be managed without a technical team.

visualImage.alt: PortCo HR Collective login page preview

sections.title: Approach:
sections.intro:
The design starts with a painting. The client brought a single piece of original artwork and asked for it to become the soul of the brand. Not decoration, but the visual foundation everything else draws from. The artwork informed the entire visual system, shaping the logo, typography, color palette, and interface design across the platform.

Built on top of that identity:
items: A gated member directory, insights hub, and events platform with passwordless magic-link login
A self-managed Webflow CMS that allows the client to publish content, manage members, and update events without any technical support
Automated workflows that reduce manual administration by keeping member data and content synchronized across platforms

sections.title: Outcome:
sections.intro: A distinctive membership platform that gives the community a credible digital presence while keeping administration lightweight. Members get a seamless experience across content, events, and peer discovery, while automation keeps content and member information consistently up to date.

systemically.title: SystemicAlly
systemically.subtitle: A clear, professional website for a leadership and transformation consultancy

sections.title: Overview:
sections.intro:
SystemicAlly is a consulting company supporting leaders, teams, and organizations through leadership development and meaningful transformation.

The website needed to communicate the company’s expertise clearly, present its services in an approachable way, and build trust with prospective clients.

sections.title: Approach:
sections.intro:
The goal was to translate SystemicAlly’s existing visual direction into a polished, responsive website with a clear and intuitive structure.

We focused on:
items: A professional visual experience aligned with the company’s brand
Clear content hierarchy for services, programs, and areas of expertise
Flexible page layouts for detailed consulting content
Responsive development across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices
Google Analytics integration to support ongoing performance insights

sections.title: Outcome:
sections.intro:
The result is a polished and credible digital presence that reflects SystemicAlly’s expertise while keeping the experience accessible and easy to navigate.

Visitors can quickly understand the company’s approach, explore its consulting solutions, and find the right path to begin a conversation.

towarowa.title: Towarowa 41
towarowa.subtitle: A refined digital experience for a premium city apartment

sections.title: Overview:
sections.intro:
Towarowa 41 is a premium apartment rental property designed for visitors seeking a comfortable and stylish stay in the heart of the city.

The website needed to showcase the property’s unique character, highlight key amenities, and provide visitors with a seamless browsing experience across all devices.

sections.title: Approach:
sections.intro:
The goal was to create a digital experience that reflects the quality and atmosphere of the property while making information easy to find.

We focused on:
items: A clean, elegant visual design inspired by boutique hospitality brands
Large, high-quality imagery to showcase the apartment and its surroundings
Clear presentation of amenities, accessibility information, and local attractions
An integrated booking system for a straightforward reservation experience
Responsive layouts optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices

sections.title: Outcome:
sections.intro:
The result is a modern and sophisticated website that effectively presents the property while maintaining a simple and intuitive user experience.

Visitors can quickly explore the accommodation, discover nearby points of interest, access the information they need, and complete their booking through a clear reservation flow.

metrics.description: estimated increase in direct booking enquiries following the website launch
saved each month by reducing manual booking coordination and repetitive guest enquiries

sections.title: Before:
sections.intro: Expenses were tracked manually. Receipts arrived by email and post. As a result:
items: Receipts were processed manually with high risk of errors.
Files were stored inconsistently across folders.
Manual data entry into Excel led to missing receipts and delays.

sections.title: After:
sections.intro: Receipts are now sent via email or Telegram and processed automatically.
items: Images/PDFs are extracted and cleaned via OCR.
Date, amount, currency, and vendor are identified with AI.
Files are renamed and stored in the correct OneDrive monthly folder.
Data is added into the correct Excel table (EUR or CHF).
Everything stays organized & ready for reimbursement review.

sections.title: Impact:
sections.intro: A messy monthly task became a clean, reliable, hands-off workflow.
items: ~70% less manual admin time
Fewer mistakes and missing receipts
Consistent file naming + structured archive
Faster workflows with less frustration

testimonial.quote: We were spending a significant amount of time processing receipts and expenses manually. The automation now extracts the information, files the documents, and updates our records automatically, saving us hours of work every month. It has taken away one of the most repetitive administrative tasks in our firm and we are incredibly grateful to the Moniré team for delivering such a practical and effective solution.
testimonial.author: Margaret Rikhof

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how Moniré ("we", "our", "us") collects, uses, and protects your information when you visit our website or interact with our services.

sections.title: Information We Collect
sections.body: We collect the following types of information:
items: Usage Data: Through Google Analytics, we collect anonymised website usage information such as device type, browser, pages visited, time spent on pages, and general location (city or region). This data does not identify you personally.
Contact form data: When you submit our contact form, we collect your name, email address, and any additional information you choose to provide.

Client brief form downloads: When you click to download our client brief form, we may track anonymous analytics data (e.g., number of downloads). We do not collect personal information unless you later send the completed brief back to us.

sections.title: How We Use Your Information
items: Improve our website and user experience.
Respond to your inquiries and communicate with you.
Review information you voluntarily provide in a client brief form to prepare proposals or services.
Maintain website performance, analytics, and security.

sections.body: If you are located in the EU/EEA, the UK, or another GDPR-relevant region, we process your data based on:

Legitimate interests for analytics, website optimisation, and security.
Contractual necessity when communicating with you about potential or ongoing work.
sections.after: You can control cookies through your browser settings.

sections.title: Data Storage and Security
sections.body: We store personal data securely and restrict access to authorised persons only. We keep your data only for as long as necessary for the purposes outlined in this policy. We do not sell or rent your personal information.

sections.title: Sharing Your Information

items: Required by law.
Necessary to respond to enquiries (for example, using email service providers).
Needed to deliver requested services, such as preparing a proposal.

Withdraw your consent at any time.
Request restriction of processing.
Request data portability.

website-builders-vs-custom-development.contentHtml:
One of the easiest ways for a website project to become expensive or frustrating is choosing the wrong platform too early.

We've worked across many different website builders and built fully custom coded websites and applications. Here's how we actually think through the decision.

There's no single platform that's right for every business. The right choice depends on what your site needs to do, who needs to manage it, and where the business is heading.

We start with what the site needs to do

Before we look at any platform, we want to understand the job the website has to do.

A simple five-page site for a consultant has very different requirements to a membership platform, a booking-heavy service business, or a site that needs to connect to external tools. The platform choice follows the requirements. Not the other way around.

Some things we ask early on:

Will you be updating the site yourself, or will someone else manage it? How often will the content change? Does it need to connect to any other tools? How important is design quality to the brand? Is SEO performance a priority?

The answers shape everything that follows.

Why we often choose Webflow

A lot of the websites we build are marketing sites, service-based business sites, or CMS-driven sites that need to look great, perform well, and stay that way without ongoing technical work. That's where Webflow tends to stand out.

The biggest practical advantage is that Webflow maintains the platform for you. There are no plugins to update, no security patches to apply, no risk of something breaking because two tools stopped working together. Day to day it runs without anyone needing to babysit it.

Performance is also genuinely strong. Webflow sites load quickly, are built with clean code, and are structured in a way that search engines handle well. That's not always the case with platforms that rely heavily on third-party plugins to add functionality.

On the design side, Webflow gives us more flexibility than most builders. Every site we build looks and feels unique to that business, not like a template with a logo swapped in.

For many businesses, the cost structure is also simpler and more predictable than platforms that rely heavily on third-party plugins and ongoing maintenance work.

We'd suggest Webflow when design quality matters, performance and SEO are priorities, and the business wants a site that runs reliably without needing constant attention.

For most small businesses, the right platform is one that looks great, runs reliably, and does not need constant technical maintenance.

A note on WordPress

WordPress powers a huge part of the internet and we've built with it too. For content-heavy sites or businesses already deeply invested in the WordPress ecosystem, it can still be a reasonable option.

That said, it's not our first recommendation. The main reason is maintenance. Plugins need updating, security vulnerabilities come up, and without regular attention things can break or slow down in ways that aren't always obvious. For small teams that don't want to think about technical upkeep, that overhead adds up and the ongoing costs are easy to underestimate at the start.

A well-built WordPress site can work well. But in our experience, for most small businesses there are better options available now.

When custom development makes sense

Sometimes a project goes beyond what any website builder is designed for. If a business needs highly custom backend logic, complex integrations, application-like functionality, or advanced user systems, custom development often becomes the better option.

For those more complex projects, we typically build with modern frameworks like React or Next.js to support custom logic, performance, and long-term scalability.

The tradeoff is time, cost, and ongoing maintenance responsibility. Not every business needs a fully custom build, even if it sounds impressive. In fact, many businesses are better served by a simpler system their team can realistically manage long-term.

What we're actually trying to balance

We care less about using the most popular platform and more about choosing something that fits the business properly.

A beautiful website doesn't help much if updating it becomes stressful. A highly custom setup isn't always a good thing if it creates unnecessary complexity. And the cheapest option upfront isn't always the cheapest over time.

Most of the time we're trying to find the right balance between flexibility, ease of use, performance, maintainability, cost, and how the business actually operates day to day.

The question that matters most

A lot of platform decisions get framed as technical debates, but for most businesses the real question is much simpler:

  • Will this still work well for the team two to three years from now?
  • Will people feel comfortable updating it?
  • Will it become harder or more expensive to manage over time?

Those questions usually matter more than which platform happens to be popular right now.

what-ai-automation-actually-means-for-a-.contentHtml:
If you've been hearing a lot about AI lately and wondering whether any of it applies to you, you're not alone.

Most of the conversation around AI automation is aimed at enterprise companies with large budgets and dedicated tech teams. For a small business owner, it can feel expensive and overly technical.

But in practice, the most valuable automations for small businesses are often very simple. They're the repetitive tasks teams are doing manually every day that quietly eat up hours each week.

It's not about replacing people

The most common concern we hear is that automation means people will lose their jobs or decisions will get handed over to a machine. That's not what we build.

Every workflow we create keeps a human in the loop. The AI handles the repetitive, time-consuming parts. The person reviews, confirms, and stays in control. The goal is to make sure your team's time and judgment goes toward work that actually needs it.

What it looks like in practice

Here are three examples from work we've done with real clients.

1. Expense receipts

One client was spending part of every month filing expense receipts by hand, chasing emails, renaming files, entering numbers into spreadsheets. It was slow, error-prone, and nobody enjoyed doing it.

Now receipts arrive by email, get read automatically, and land in the right folder with the right information pulled out. The team reviews and confirms. That's it.

The result was a faster, more reliable process with fewer errors and a consistent archive that's always ready for review.

~70% less time on receipt adminA small workflow change with measurable operational impact.

Read the Expense Receipts case study

2. Client onboarding

When a client says yes to a project, there's a predictable set of things that need to happen. A contract needs to go out, an onboarding email needs to be sent, folders need to be created, tasks need to be set up internally.

It's not complicated, but it takes time and it's easy to miss a step.

With the right automation in place, all of that happens automatically the moment a project is confirmed. Every time, without anyone having to remember.

3. Community membership

When someone applies to join a private community and gets accepted, their account needs to be created across multiple platforms, and those platforms don't naturally talk to each other.

Without automation, that means logging into each one separately and entering the same details manually.

With a connected workflow, acceptance triggers the setup across every platform automatically. No copy-pasting, no manual setup, and much less risk of something being missed.

The common pattern

All three examples follow the same pattern:

Something happens, the same steps follow every time, and someone used to do all of it by hand.

That's where automation tends to help most.

Not creative decisions. Not judgment calls. Just the repetitive, predictable tasks that quietly eat up time.

Automate the repetition, keep human judgment where it matters.

Is it complicated to set up?

It doesn't have to be.

We mainly build workflows with n8n, which connects to the tools your business already uses, including email, spreadsheets, cloud storage, and CRMs.

There's no need to replace your existing setup or learn an entirely new way of working.

The right automation fits around how you already work, not the other way around.

Where to start

The best place to start is usually the task you do the most often and enjoy the least.

If you find yourself:

  • copying information between tools
  • sending the same emails repeatedly
  • creating the same folders or documents
  • manually setting people up across platforms
  • chasing small administrative tasks every week

there's a good chance part of that process could be automated.

Often, the best automation opportunities are not huge systems. They are small workflows that remove a few repetitive steps from your week.

why-your-website-might-be-losing-you-cli.contentHtml:
Most business owners know their website isn't perfect. Fewer realise it might be actively costing them clients.

The problem is that a website can look fine and still be failing. It can be live, reasonably well designed, and totally invisible to the people you're trying to reach. Or visible, but doing nothing to convince them to get in touch.

Here are seven signs to look out for.

1. Your hero section doesn't explain what you do

The hero is the first thing someone sees when they land on your site. You have a few seconds to answer one question: what does this business actually do?

Most hero sections fail this test. They lead with a tagline that sounds good but says nothing. "Empowering businesses to grow." "Your success is our mission." "Taking things to the next level."

None of those tell a visitor what you do, who you do it for, or why they should stay.

A simple test: cover your logo and show the page to someone who doesn't know your business. Can they tell what you do within five seconds? If not, your hero needs work.

2. The content is about you, not your client

This is the most common mistake, and the hardest one to self-diagnose.

"We are a leading provider of..." "We have over 20 years of experience..." "We are passionate about..."

Your visitors don't arrive wondering about you. They arrive with a problem. They want to know whether you can solve it.

The shift is simple in theory but hard in practice. Instead of "We build websites for small businesses," try "Get a website that actually brings in clients." Same information, completely different focus.

Read through your homepage and count how many sentences start with "we." Then rewrite them from the client's perspective.

3. There's no clear call to action

If someone reads your site and wants to take the next step, what do they do?

If the answer isn't immediately obvious, you're losing people. Visitors won't hunt around for a way to contact you. They'll leave.

Every page should have one clear primary action. Not three. Not a contact button buried in the footer alongside six other links. One clear next step that tells the visitor exactly what to do and what to expect when they do it.

Not sure whether your site gives visitors a clear next step? It's one of the first things we look at when we work with a new client.

One clear next step on every page beats five competing choices.

4. It breaks on mobile

More than 60% of web traffic comes from phones. If your site doesn't work properly on mobile, you're losing more than half your potential visitors before they've even read a word.

This isn't just about things looking slightly different on a smaller screen. Buttons that are too small to tap, text that runs off the edge, images that don't resize, menus that don't open. All of these tell a visitor the site wasn't built with them in mind.

Pull out your phone and go through your site properly. Not a quick glance. Actually try to use it the way a new visitor would.

5. It loads too slowly

Most people will leave a page that takes more than three seconds to load. They won't wait and they won't come back.

Slow sites lose visitors before the design, copy, or photography have a chance to do their job. This is especially true on mobile, where people are often browsing with less patience and weaker connections.

If your site feels slow, or if visitors seem to drop off before engaging, it is worth looking into. Small technical improvements can often make a significant difference. But if your site is slow because of heavy templates, unnecessary plugins, or a setup that is difficult to maintain, it may be worth reconsidering the platform behind it.

6. It doesn't show up on Google or AI search

A website being live does not mean people can find it.

Search engines like Google, and increasingly AI tools like ChatGPT, need to be able to read, understand, and index your site before they can show it to anyone. If the technical foundations are not in place, your site may be effectively invisible, even to people who are actively looking for what you offer.

Most business owners never check this. They assume that because the site is up, people can find it. Often that's not the case.

A simple way to think about it: how would a new client find you if they had never heard of you? If the only way someone can reach your site is by already knowing your name, your website isn't doing enough work.

7. Your contact form goes nowhere

This one sounds unlikely but we have seen it on real client sites more than once.

Forms that were never properly connected to an email address. Inboxes that nobody checks anymore. Confirmation messages that go straight to spam. A potential client fills in the form, waits for a response, hears nothing, and moves on.

Simple test: submit your own form today.If you don't receive the enquiry, your visitors probably don't either.

Quick website self-check

If you are not sure whether your website is helping or hurting your business, start with these questions:

  • Can a stranger understand what you do within five seconds?
  • Is your main call to action easy to find?
  • Does your homepage speak more about your client's needs than your company?
  • Does the site work smoothly on mobile?
  • Does it load quickly enough to feel easy to use?
  • Can new clients find you through search or AI tools?
  • Does your contact form actually deliver enquiries?

If you answered no to several of these, your website may be quietly costing you enquiries.

Where to go from here

You don't have to fix everything at once. Start with the issue most likely to be costing you clients right now.

At Moniré, we help small and mid-sized businesses identify what is working, what is not, and what would make the biggest difference first.
